documents.title: Chronic Care Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Six-month check on his chronic issues. February labs reviewed with him: creatinine at baseline, lithium in range, sodium normal.

NDI: still drinking a lot, up twice a night; no dizzy spells since he started keeping water with him everywhere. Bipolar disorder: steady, nothing to report. Uses Tylenol only. Traveling less this quarter.

Exam: well. Mucous membranes moist. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema, no tremor.

A/P
- CKD 3a: stable. NSAID avoidance reinforced.
- NDI: drink to thirst; call early with any GI illness.
- Bipolar disorder on lithium 300 mg BID: continue; next labs with the October physical.

RTC October.

orders.reason: dehydration from gastroenteritis with nephrogenic diabetes insipidus

procedures.procedure: Telehealth visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Video Visit — Vomiting and Diarrhea
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video visit, pt at home. Called this morning.

Since Sunday night: vomiting several times a day and watery diarrhea, maybe 6-8 times a day. No blood, no fever he's measured. Can keep down sips but with his NDI he's still urinating large amounts and can't drink enough to keep up. Lightheaded when he stands. Mouth dry. Last void dilute as always.

On video: tired-appearing, lips dry, speaking full sentences, oriented.

A/P: Viral gastroenteritis with dehydration in a man with nephrogenic DI who loses free water continuously — high risk of getting behind.
- Home IV hydration through home infusion agency: normal saline 1 L over 2 h twice daily x 5 days. Agency to place a peripheral IV this afternoon.
- Ondansetron 4 mg ODT q8h prn so he can drink.
- Keep taking lithium.
- Call if he can't keep anything down, has fainting, confusion or blood in stool.

documents.title: Home infusion nurse report
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home infusion RN called: 22g PIV placed L forearm yesterday afternoon, first liter in without problem, second at bedtime. Pt still with loose stools but vomiting less, took ondansetron x2. Agency visiting daily. Will call with concerns.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (outside, received)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 06/23/2025. Copy to primary care.

CC: weak and worn out x 2 days.

HPI: 44M with CKD, bipolar disorder on lithium and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus. Developed a stomach bug about a week ago; his PCP arranged home IV fluids for dehydration, which he has been getting twice a day through a home infusion service. GI symptoms are much better, but for two days he has felt profoundly weak and fatigued. No chest pain, no shortness of breath, no fever.

History per patient and prior records: CKD; bipolar disorder; nephrogenic DI; ciguatera poisoning last year. Appendectomy. Meds: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID; normal saline 1 L IV BID at home; ondansetron prn. NKDA.

Exam: BP 130/85, HR 88, afebrile. Comfortable. Mucous membranes moist, skin turgor normal. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Neuro nonfocal.

Labs: Na 140, K 3.9, Cl 115, HCO3 18, BUN 29, Cr 2.1, glucose 98. ABG pH 7.32 / pCO2 40 / pO2 98.

MDM: Normal anion gap acidosis with chloride 115 after several days of large-volume normal saline. Volume status now replete. Picture fits hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis from excess saline.

Plan: home saline discontinued — agency notified; peripheral IV removed here. Oral fluids encouraged, tolerated well in the department. Discharged home. Follow up with PCP within 2-3 days for repeat chemistry. Return for worsening weakness, confusion, or inability to drink.

Dx: Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis due to excess normal saline infusion.

documents.title: Home infusion agency
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Home infusion agency called: ED notified them yesterday to stop the saline; IV was pulled in the ED. Remaining bags picked up this morning. Orders closed on their end. Pt has follow-up here Thursday.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Post-ED Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Seen in the ED Monday for weakness after five days of home normal saline — chloride 115, bicarb 18, pH 7.32, creatinine 2.1. Diagnosed with hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis from the saline; infusions stopped.

Today: energy coming back. No vomiting since last Thursday, stools formed since the weekend. Eating normally, drinking his usual large volumes by mouth. No dizziness standing. Taking lithium as usual. No ondansetron since Saturday.

Exam: looks well. Moist mucosa. Heart regular. Lungs clear. Abd soft, nontender. Former IV site L forearm clean, no cord or redness.

A/P
1. Hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis — repeat BMP today.
2. Gastroenteritis and dehydration — resolved.
3. CKD 3a / NDI / lithium — creatinine on today's panel; lithium level with the next routine set.

Repeat BMP in two weeks.

documents.title: Yesterday's labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Better already: chloride down to 109 and bicarbonate up to 22 (from 115 and 18 in the ED). Creatinine 1.9, coming back toward your usual. Keep drinking normally — no extra salt tablets or sports-drink loading needed. Recheck on the 10th.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
44M, yearly exam.

Interval: June gastroenteritis treated with home IV saline, then ED visit for hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis — resolved by the July recheck. Feels fully himself since. Mood stable; PHQ-9 1. NDI unchanged, drinking to thirst. Expects to be traveling more again next year.

Meds: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID. NKDA.
SH: never smoker; 2-3 drinks/wk.

Exam: well-appearing. HEENT normal. Neck supple, no thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. No edema. Neuro nonfocal. No tremor. Skin without lesions of concern.

A/P
- CKD 3a, NDI, bipolar disorder on lithium: CMP, lithium level, TSH, UA, urine albumin/creatinine today. No change.
- Colorectal cancer screening: turns 45 in April. Prefers stool testing to colonoscopy — FIT kit to go out in the spring.
- Lipids today. Flu and COVID at a nurse visit later this month.

RTC 1 year; labs in January.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Admission History and Physical (outside, received)
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Regional hospital, biocontainment intensive care unit. Admission 06/20/2026. Sent to primary care at their request.

Reason for admission: fever and GI illness after travel to Guinea, with high-risk exposure.

HPI: 45-year-old man (CKD, bipolar disorder on lithium carbonate, nephrogenic DI; past ciguatera poisoning and saline-related hyperchloremic acidosis) came home to the US a week ago from a month of business travel in Guinea, in both cities and rural districts. While there he went to a funeral, had close contact with relatives of the person who died and helped wash and prepare the body. Now with fever, diffuse abdominal pain and many episodes of non-bloody emesis and watery stool, plus myalgias, malaise and sore throat. He did not eat undercooked meat and did not swim or wade in fresh water. His PCP and public health were in contact before arrival; he came by EMS directly into isolation.

Meds: lithium carbonate 300 mg BID. Allergies: NKDA. Never smoker, social alcohol.

Exam: T 39.2 C, HR 110, BP 96/64, RR 22. Acutely ill, dry. Conjunctivae injected. Posterior pharynx mildly red. Heart tachycardic, regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen tender throughout, no rebound, no guarding. No rash, no petechiae, no bleeding from any site. Alert, no focal deficit.

Initial labs: WBC 3.1, platelets 82, AST 286, ALT 174, creatinine 2.4. Malaria rapid antigen negative, thick and thin smears without parasites. Blood cultures sent.

Assessment: suspected viral hemorrhagic fever given the funeral exposure. Full biocontainment precautions. Supportive care started while confirmatory testing is run with the state laboratory.

Addendum 06/21: Ebola virus RT-PCR on blood DETECTED (Zaire). Ansuvimab given as a single infusion today. Lithium held while volume status and kidney function are unstable. Public health notified; contact tracing under way.

documents.title: Discharge Summary (outside, received)
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Regional hospital — biocontainment ICU, Infectious Disease service.
Admitted 06/20/2026. Discharged 07/09/2026.

Principal diagnosis: Ebola virus disease (Zaire ebolavirus), confirmed by blood RT-PCR 06/21.
Other problems: chronic kidney disease; bipolar disorder on lithium; nephrogenic diabetes insipidus; history of ciguatera poisoning.

Course: Presented febrile, tachycardic and hypotensive with vomiting and diarrhea after funeral exposure in Guinea. Malaria testing negative; blood cultures no growth. Received ansuvimab 50 mg/kg IV once on 06/21. Supportive care with IV balanced crystalloid (chosen over saline given his prior saline-related acidosis), electrolyte replacement and antiemetics; strict intake/output given his NDI. Lithium held from admission. GI losses slowed over the first week; fever resolved by 06/28. Thrombocytopenia, leukopenia and transaminase elevation improved steadily without bleeding. Creatinine 2.4 on arrival, 1.8 at discharge. Blood RT-PCR not detected 07/06 and 07/08; released from isolation by the infection prevention team and public health.

Discharge labs (07/08): WBC 5.4, platelets 206, AST 44, ALT 61, creatinine 1.8.
Discharge vitals: T 36.8, HR 78, BP 118/74, RR 16.

Discharge medications: RESUME lithium carbonate 300 mg BID.

Survivor instructions: Use condoms for every sexual contact for at least 12 months from illness onset or until two semen tests are negative. Semen testing through our ID survivor clinic, starting about three months from onset. Eye exam with ophthalmology in the coming weeks. Report eye pain, redness or vision change promptly.

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week (lithium level and chemistry); ID survivor clinic in about one month.

events.reason: Eye exam after Ebola virus disease

documents.title: Ophthalmology Letter (outside, received)
documents.author: ophthalmology
documents.body:
Outside ophthalmology practice. Date of visit 08/05/2026.

Thank you for sending Mr. Bradley, a 45-year-old man seen for a screening examination about seven weeks after Ebola virus disease. He has no eye pain, redness, floaters, light sensitivity or change in vision.

Visual acuity 20/20 in each eye uncorrected. Pupils equal and reactive, no afferent defect. Intraocular pressures normal. Slit lamp: lids and conjunctivae quiet, corneas clear, anterior chambers deep and quiet without cell or flare, lenses clear. Dilated fundus exam: vitreous clear, discs sharp with healthy rims, maculae and vessels normal, peripheral retina flat without lesions, both eyes.

Impression: normal eye examination; no evidence of uveitis.

Plan: no treatment. He should return promptly for any eye pain, redness or blurring. Routine follow-up otherwise.

Ophthalmology

documents.title: ID Survivor Clinic Letter (outside, received)
documents.author: infectious disease
documents.body:
Infectious Disease survivor clinic, regional hospital. Visit date 08/12/2026.

Mr. Bradley returns about one month after discharge from our biocontainment unit for Ebola virus disease (onset mid-June 2026). He reports his energy is coming back steadily; he is working from home full days and walking daily. No fevers, eye symptoms, hearing change or new joint complaints. Back on lithium without trouble. Normal eye exam with ophthalmology last week reviewed. Your July labs reviewed.

Exam today unremarkable.

Plan:
- Semen Ebola RNA testing to begin at three months from onset, in September 2026, then monthly until two consecutive negatives.
- Continue condom use with any sexual contact until then, and for at least 12 months from onset.
- Return to our clinic after the first semen result.

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care.
Infectious Disease
